answer: Sybil resistance comes from bonding each identity in a collateral escrow and linking equivocation evidence across the swarm: when k coordinated identities sign conflicting statements, pairwise correlated evidence produces penalties scaling as O(k²), not merely k. Detection applies an exponential multiplier to aggregate capital loss, while asymmetric depreciation makes recovered collateral worth less than the amount at risk. Thus identities named umber, haven, and mesa cannot cheaply divide one operator’s stake to evade accountability.
